selection: The same three posts from the completed manual follow-up, including one with no encoded entities. No new source selection or detector-score selection.
intervention: Rust emits the raw text, all entities decoded, each occurrence decoded alone, and all occurrences decoded except each one. The entity-free source has one unchanged variant. The only substitution is literal   to U+00A0; all variants must render to the same control text.
manual_scope: The three full source texts and original comparisons were already read. This follow-up inspected every distinct changed annotation among matched tokens wholly within the unchanged prefix before the first entity, added token spans there, and the affected sentence-boundary evidence. Other variant annotations were not exhaustively judged.

findings.observation: Decoding either of the first two entities alone reproduces the earlier erroneous result-coordination analysis in unchanged preceding text. Decoding any of the other three alone does not. Some combinations also change an elliptical fragment's root; that fragment permits competing analyses and is not counted as a proven regression.
findings.tokenization_caution: Decoding the first entity exposes a preceding word and period as separate tokens. Original tokens crossing the prefix boundary are outside the matched-token comparison, so added prefix spans are reported separately.

findings.observation: Only the fully decoded variant removes the two inspected content-sentence starts before the trailing entities. None of the five single substitutions or five all-except-one variants removes them. The affected independent question and closing sentence become clausal complements of an earlier question's predicate.
findings.qualification: This establishes an interaction among the tested changes. It does not exhaust all subsets, prove a globally minimal cause, or establish a relationship to detector scores. Other changed tags and relations include improvements inside an already incorrect merged span.

findings.observation: The entity-free source reproduces its prior annotations exactly. All rendered controls across all sources also reproduce their prior token and sentence arrays, including known errors.

interpretation: Consistent input rendering removes sensitivity to these alternative entity spellings in this comparison, but the common rendered parse still contains grammatical errors. Single-edit probes would miss the observed boundary interaction. A feature pipeline needs a fixed input policy and separate manual syntax validation.
limitations: This is a targeted development diagnostic on previously inspected posts. It does not estimate corpus-wide robustness, validate an English grammar, demonstrate better A accuracy, or certify gradients for B. Linux execution has not been qualified for the new example.
